title: Neutron contribution to the force on a proton vortex in superconducting neutron-star matter
authors: Oleg A. Goglichidze, Mikhail E. Gusakov
abstract: We investigate the forces acting on a proton vortex in superconducting neutron-star matter composed of neutrons, protons, and electrons, accounting for Fermi-liquid interactions in the neutron-proton subsystem. While the force arising from electron scattering by the vortex magnetic field is well known, we demonstrate that normal neutrons also exert a force on proton vortices due to Fermi-liquid coupling with superconducting protons. Using a kinetic approach based on Landau Fermi-liquid theory, we show that neutron quasiparticles scatter off a proton vortex through the spatially varying condensate momentum, giving rise to a longitudinal force proportional to the relative neutron-vortex velocity. In contrast to the electron contribution, this force has no transverse component and vanishes in the absence of neutron-proton Fermi-liquid interaction. Within a simple model, we analyze the main properties of this force and provide physically motivated estimates of its magnitude.
summary: This paper calculates the force acting on a proton vortex embedded in superconducting neutron star material. It specifically derives and quantifies a previously uncounted longitudinal force component arising from normal neutrons interacting via Fermi-liquid coupling with superconducting protons. This work advances our understanding of vortex dynamics in compact objects by incorporating these subtle quantum mechanical interactions.
main_problem: The study investigates the additional force exerted on a proton vortex within superconducting neutron-star matter due to interactions with normal neutrons.
main_result: Normal neutrons contribute a new longitudinal force component to the vortex force, which is proportional to the relative neutron-vortex velocity and vanishes without Fermi-liquid coupling.
method: The analysis employs a kinetic approach derived from Landau Fermi-liquid theory applied to the neutron-proton subsystem interactions.
model_or_system: The system modeled is dense matter inside a neutron star, comprising superconducting protons, normal neutrons, and electrons. The physics involves type-II superconductivity characterized by magnetic vortices.
key_observables: Total force on the vortex ($F_{m	o v}$), which is expected to be longitudinal and velocity-dependent.
important_parameters: Temperature relative to critical temperatures ($T_{cn} < T < T_{cp}$); characteristic length scales like coherence length ($\xi$) and London penetration depth ($\lambda$).
main_assumptions: Protons are superconducting while neutrons are normal; the vortex core is treated as infinitely thin, and quasiparticle collisions are neglected.
paper_structure: The paper develops the force calculation by analyzing momentum conservation laws ($\partial P_i / \partial t + \partial \Pi_{ik} / \partial r_k = ...$) and decomposing the total force into contributions from different particle species, culminating in the derivation of the neutron contribution $\mathbf{F}^{(np)}_i$.
why_interesting: The application of Fermi-liquid theory to determine transport forces in extreme astrophysical environments like neutron stars provides a rich example of non-equilibrium many-body physics relevant to dense matter dynamics.
